mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior month predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower interest rates reduce the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows and stimulate economic activity.
failure_condition: In the 20-day forward period following a FEDFUNDS decline of at least 0.25 percentage points, the S&P 500 produces negative returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS is above 4.5%, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of weak employment growth (PAYEMS growth rate below 0.1% monthly) and rising unemployment (UNRATE increase > 0.2 percentage points) signals a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where PAYEMS growth is below 0.1% and UNRATE rises by more than 0.2pp, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a housing boom (HOUST above 1000 thousand units) signals strong consumer demand and economic momentum, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods, when HOUST exceeds 1000, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95 (index, 2017=100) signals an imminent recession, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as market participants react to weakening economic activity.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 95, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A positive quarterly growth rate in real GDP (GDPC1) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as stronger economic growth supports corporate earnings and reduces the risk of recession.
failure_condition: In periods of positive quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1), the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3% annualized) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 4%) signals an overheating economy that prompts aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL exceeds 3% and UNRATE is below 4%, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 6%), a decline in unemployment (UNRATE decrease > 0.3 percentage points) signals a potential economic recovery, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate Fed easing and improved consumer spending.
failure_condition: In high-unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 6%), when UNRATE declines by more than 0.3pp, the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases.
